div.head: II Ew 1.1
div.ab: He agsode hy þa, hwa to ðære bote cyrran wolde ⁊ on ðære geferræddenne beon ðe he wære, ⁊ þæt lufian ðæt he lufode, ⁊ ðæt ascunian ðæt he ascunode, ægðer ge on sæ ge on lande.
He agsode hy ða, hwa to ðære bote cyrran wolde ⁊ on ðære geferrædene beon ðe he wære, ⁊ þæt lufian þæt he lufode, ⁊ þæt ascunian þæt he ascunode, ægðær ge on sæ ge on lande.
Inquisiuit itaque, qui ad emendationem uelit redire et in societate permanere qua ipse sit, et amare quod amet, et nolle quod nolit, in mari et in terra.
He agsode hy þa, hwa to ðære bote cyrran wolde ⁊ on ðære geferræddenne beon ðe he wære, ⁊ þæt lufian ðæt he lufode, ⁊ ðæt ascunian ðæt he ascunode, ægðer ge on sæ ge on lande.

Er fragte sie nun, wer sich zu dieser Besserung bekehren wolle und zu der Gefährtenschaft, wo er sei, gehören und das, was er liebe, lieben und was er meide, meiden [wolle], sowohl zur See wie zu Lande.
He asked them then who would turn to this amendment and belong to the fellowship where he was, and love what he loved and shun what he shunned, both at sea and on land.

He asked which of them would devote themselves to this [work of] reformation and which of them would cooperate with him in his efforts, favouring what he favoured and discountenancing what he discountenanced, both by land and sea.

note.seg: Nicht ‘der Busse unterwerfen’, sondern der Reform
Not ‘submit to the compensation’, but to the reform

Das Wort übs. comitatus der Vulgata Gen. 50, 9 oder steht für die ‘societas eines Konvents’ oder für ‘Gilde’ oder für ‘Kriegsgefolge’: Ælfhelm testiert für Kirche, Verwandte, Herrn und minan geferan, þe me midridað; Bi 1306. Letzterem steht der hier gemeinte ‘Vassallenverband’ zunächst. Vgl. Gl Gefolge 13b; Mannschaftseid 2. 5. Nach Brunner Zs. Savigny RG, Germ. 1914, 457 fordert Ew nur zur Königstreue (s. d. Gl 7) auf, bedeutet geferræden nur ‘Friedens- und Rechtsgenossenschaft’. Ich sehe in dieser Verpflichtung wohl einen Übergang vom Gefolgseid zum allgemeinen Untertaneneide bei III Em, aber, ebenso wie in V As 3, noch nicht diesen selbst. Nur die Witan sollen Königsvassallen werden

The word translates comitatus of the Vulgate Gen. 50, 9, or stands for the ‘societas of a convent’, or for ‘guild’, or for ‘war-band’: Ælfhelm makes bequests to church, kinsmen, lord and minan geferan, þe me midridað; Bi 1306. The ‘body of vassals’ meant here is closest to the last of these. Cf. Gl Gefolge 13b; Mannschaftseid 2. 5. According to Brunner Zs. Savigny RG, Germ. 1914, 457, Ew merely calls for loyalty to the king (see that word in Gl 7), and geferræden means only ‘association in peace and law’. In this obligation I do indeed see a transition from the retainer’s oath to the general oath of subjects in III Em, but, just as in V As 3, not yet that oath itself. Only the witan are to become the king’s vassals
